candidates.tagline: OpenAI spent $6.4 billion on design talent. First product: a $350 squirmy donut.
candidates.story: OpenAI acquired Jony Ive's design studio for $6.4 billion in 2025, assembled a 200-person hardware team, and unveiled its first product on August 6: a hockey-puck-sized ring speaker with no screen and 'moving parts for personality,' priced at $300–$400 and launching in 2027 — critics immediately compared it to the failed $699 Humane AI Pin.
candidates.why_funny: The world's most hyped AI company paid iPhone-designer money to put a hole in a speaker and give it fidget-toy features.
candidates.alt: Concept render of the OpenAI speaker — a fabric-covered donut/ring shape shown in a hand alongside diagrams labelled Spin, Tilt, and Click, with OpenAI logo and text reading 'Moving parts that help give it personality'

candidates.tagline: $2.79 billion, 26 lanes, traffic 51% worse. Houston is planning a $13 billion sequel.
candidates.story: Houston widened I-10 (the Katy Freeway) to 26 lanes at a cost of $2.79 billion between 2003 and 2008, making it the world's widest highway; within three years commute times had increased by up to 51% due to induced demand — and the city is now pursuing a $13 billion expansion of nearby I-45, rerunning the same experiment at four times the cost.
candidates.why_funny: They spent three billion dollars making the world's widest road to reduce traffic, traffic got worse, and the plan is now to make a nearby road even wider for $13 billion.
candidates.alt: The Katy Freeway (I-10) in Houston showing massive gridlock across many lanes of traffic with elevated interchange ramps converging overhead, demonstrating the induced demand problem the $2.79 billion expansion was meant to solve
